title: Relative product theorem
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{k_0}$. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] for these parameters, with its categories $D^b_{ctf}(-,\Lambda)$, derived tensor and pullback, compact-support image, and the supplied axioms (A1)--(A6). Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $f:X\to B$, $g:Y\to B$ separated finite type, $\pi_X,\pi_Y$ the
projections of $X\times_BY$ (so $f\times_Bg=g\circ \pi_Y$), and put $K\boxtimes L=\pi_X^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda \pi_Y^*L$ for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$.
Define the canonical map as the composite of the inverse of the
composition isomorphism $Rg_!R\pi_{Y!}\cong R(f\times_Bg)_!$ of (A4), the inverse
of the projection transformation of [def-sf-pf] for $\pi_Y$ at $(\pi_X^*K,L)$, the
inverse of the base-change exchange
$\operatorname{Ex}_!:Lg^*Rf_!K\to R\pi_{Y!}L\pi_X^*K$ of (A2), the symmetry of
$\otimes^L_\Lambda$, and the inverse of the projection transformation for $g$
at $(L,Rf_!K)$ followed by the symmetry, i.e. of the four steps of the proof
below (its coherence — symmetry, triple products, base change, projection
formula — is the separate coherence lemma for the relative product). Then this
canonical map

$$
R(f\times_Bg)_!\bigl(K\boxtimes L\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda Rg_!L
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $K$ and $L$, compatible with base change
$b:B'\to B$ for $B'$ separated of finite type over $k$, finite reduction, scalar extension, and with the
identifications $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$. For $B=\operatorname{Spec}k$
and closed immersions $i_Z:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $i_W:W\hookrightarrow Y$,
it gives the compact-support product on the closed subschemes:

$$
R\Gamma_c(Z,i_Z^*K)\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Gamma_c(W,i_W^*L)
\cong R\Gamma_c(Z\times_kW,(i_Z\times i_W)^*(K\boxtimes L)).
$$

This is cohomology of the restrictions to the closed subschemes.
Cohomology with supports $R\Gamma_Z(X,K)=R\Gamma(Z,Ri_Z^!K)$ is a different
object from $R\Gamma_c(Z,i_Z^*K)$. The absolute supports formula is treated separately in the purity and duality chapters. Over a general base $B$ the supports version
fails, so only the compact-support form is stated relatively.

proof.text: Use relative_product_presentation_exists for existence. Compose the six isomorphisms in their defined order. Their hom components are isomorphisms by typeclass inference, and naturality is the naturality equation for this natural transformation at Prod.mkHom a b.

Apply relative_product_coefficient_factor_squares. Regard each of its six equations as a CommSq and paste them with CommSq.horiz_comp. Functor.map_comp and the hom of an Iso.trans identify the resulting equation with coefficient compatibility of relativeKunnethMap.

Take proper-coordinate existence from its stated theorem. Construct the identity coefficient comparison on R, with identity operation comparisons; units and counits are the identity equations. Its recorded normalization follows by cancellation of tensorClosed and its inverse. Apply the coefficient/proper factor theorem to this identity comparison for ProperNormalization. Unfold the conjugated properFactors and cancel the six successive objectIso hom/inv pairs to obtain proper compatibility for any selected proper maps.

Use the cube-factor transport lemma for primitive comparison existence and its seven beta_i. Paste its six separate commuting squares by CommSq.horiz_comp. Rewrite beta_0 and beta_6 by their endpoint equations to obtain exactly the required geometric base-change square.

Apply the independent closed-fibre specialization lemma to R and J for the last clause. It uses the same six isomorphisms on the closed schemes and then the canonical point tensor comparison, without coefficient or cube compatibility.

In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $B$ be a separated finite-type

projections of $X\times_BY$ (so $f\times_Bg=g\circ q$), and put $K\boxtimes L=p^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda q^*L$ for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$.
Define the canonical map as the composite of the inverse of the
composition isomorphism $Rg_!Rq_!\cong R(f\times_Bg)_!$ of (A4), the inverse
of the projection transformation of [def-sf-pf] for $q$ at $(p^*K,L)$, the
inverse of the base-change exchange
$\operatorname{Ex}_!:Lg^*Rf_!K\to Rq_!Lp^*K$ of (A2), the symmetry of
$\otimes^L_\Lambda$, and the inverse of the projection transformation for $g$
at $(L,Rf_!K)$ followed by the symmetry, i.e. of the four steps of the proof
below. Then this
canonical map

$$
R(f\times_Bg)_!\bigl(K\boxtimes L\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda Rg_!L
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $K$ and $L$, compatible with base change
$B'\to B$ and with the identifications $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$. For $B=\operatorname{Spec}k$
and closed immersions $i_Z:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $i_W:W\hookrightarrow Y$,
it gives the compact-support product on the closed subschemes:

$$
R\Gamma_c(Z,i_Z^*K)\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Gamma_c(W,i_W^*L)
\cong R\Gamma_c(Z\times_kW,(i_Z\times i_W)^*(K\boxtimes L)).
$$

This is cohomology of the restrictions to the closed subschemes.
Cohomology with supports $R\Gamma_Z(X,K)=R\Gamma(Z,Ri_Z^!K)$ is a different
object from $R\Gamma_c(Z,i_Z^*K)$; its product formula over
$\operatorname{Spec}k$ is [lem-pur-kunneth-supported]. Over a general base
$B$ the supports version fails, so only the compact-support form is stated
relatively.

proof.text:
The operations are those of [def-sf-datum] and [def-sf-pf],
cohomology with supports has its separate meaning in
[def-pur-support-cohomology].
Step 1: by (A4), $R(f\times_Bg)_!=Rg_!\circ Rq_!$, so
$R(f\times_Bg)_!(K\boxtimes L)=Rg_!\bigl(Rq_!(q^*L\otimes^L_\Lambda p^*K)\bigr)$. Step 2: the projection formula (A3) for $q$, whose target is
$Y$, gives $Rq_!(q^*L\otimes^L p^*K)\cong L\otimes^L_\Lambda Rq_!(p^*K)$.
Step 3: base change (A2) for the Cartesian square with $p,q,f,g$ gives
$Rq_!(p^*K)\cong Lg^*Rf_!K$. Step 4: applying the projection formula to
$g$ with first variable $L$ and second variable $Rf_!K$ gives
$Rg_!\bigl(L\otimes^L_\Lambda Lg^*Rf_!K\bigr)\cong Rg_!L\otimes^L_\Lambda Rf_!K$, which is the displayed isomorphism. Step 5:
apply the same formula to the separated finite-type morphisms
$Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the
pullbacks $i_Z^*K,i_W^*L$. Pullback preserves their finite-Tor
hypotheses, and the exterior product is the pullback of $K\boxtimes L$.
This proves the claimed compact-support formula on the closed subschemes.

theorem relativeKunneth
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} {C : D.CoefficientDatum}
    {E : Type u} [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E] {n : ℕ} {hn : 1 ≤ n}
    (S : SixFunctorDatum D C E n hn) (s : PodCoefficientStage)
    (Q : SixFunctorCompactifiedSquare D)
    [IsSeparated Q.Y.obj.hom] [IsSeparated Q.f.hom.left]
    [IsSeparated Q.g.hom.left] [IsSeparated Q.g'.hom.left] [IsSeparated Q.f'.hom.left]
    (cg : Compactification Q.g.hom.left)
    (ch : Compactification (Q.f' ≫ Q.g).hom.left) :
    Nonempty (RelativeProductPresentation S s Q) ∧
    ∀ R : RelativeProductPresentation S s Q,
      (∀ K L, IsIso ((relativeKunnethMap R cg ch).app (K, L))) ∧
      (∀ K K' L L' (a : K ⟶ K') (b : L ⟶ L'),
        ((relativeProductTerms Q cg ch 0).eval
          R.coordinates.operations R.coordinates.tensor).map (Prod.mkHom a b) ≫
            (relativeKunnethMap R cg ch).app (K', L') =
          (relativeKunnethMap R cg ch).app (K, L) ≫
            ((relativeProductTerms Q cg ch 6).eval
              R.coordinates.operations R.coordinates.tensor).map (Prod.mkHom a b)) ∧
      (∀ (E' : Type u) [Field E'] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E']
        [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E'] (n' : ℕ) (hn' : 1 ≤ n')
        (S' : SixFunctorDatum D C E' n' hn') (s' : PodCoefficientStage)
        (R' : RelativeProductPresentation S' s' Q) (A : RelativeProductCoefficientData R R'),
        A.RecordedComparison → ∀ K L,
          (A.functor Q.Y).map ((relativeKunnethMap R cg ch).app (K, L)) ≫
              (A.objectIso cg ch 6).hom.app (K, L) =
            (A.objectIso cg ch 0).hom.app (K, L) ≫
              (relativeKunnethMap R' cg ch).app
                ((A.functor Q.X).obj K, (A.functor Q.Y').obj L)) ∧
      (Nonempty (RelativeProductProperCoordinates R.coordinates) ∧
        ∀ J : RelativeProductProperCoordinates R.coordinates,
          R.ProperNormalization J ∧
          ∀ (q : ∀ {X Y : SixFunctorSpace D}, (X ⟶ Y) → Bool)
            (hq : ∀ {X Y : SixFunctorSpace D} (f : X ⟶ Y),
              q f = true → IsProper f.hom.left) K L,
            (relativeKunnethMap R cg ch).app (K, L) ≫
                (J.objectIso q hq (relativeProductTerms Q cg ch 6)).hom.app (K, L) =
              (J.objectIso q hq (relativeProductTerms Q cg ch 0)).hom.app (K, L) ≫
                ((R.properFactors J q hq cg ch 0 ≪≫
                  R.properFactors J q hq cg ch 1 ≪≫ R.properFactors J q hq cg ch 2 ≪≫
                  R.properFactors J q hq cg ch 3 ≪≫ R.properFactors J q hq cg ch 4 ≪≫
                  R.properFactors J q hq cg ch 5).hom.app (K, L))) ∧
      (∀ (Q' : SixFunctorCompactifiedSquare D)
        [IsSeparated Q'.g.hom.left] [IsSeparated Q'.g'.hom.left]
        [IsSeparated Q'.f'.hom.left]
        (R' : RelativeProductPresentation S s Q')
        (cg' : Compactification Q'.g.hom.left)
        (ch' : Compactification (Q'.f' ≫ Q'.g).hom.left)
        (G : RelativeKunnethCube Q Q' cg ch cg' ch'),
        Nonempty (RelativeKunnethCubeComparisons R R' G) ∧
        ∀ (A : RelativeKunnethCubeComparisons R R' G) K L,
          (R'.coordinates.operations.pull G.b G.separated_b).map
              ((relativeKunnethMap R cg ch).app (K, L)) ≫ (A.targetIso K L).hom =
            (A.sourceIso K L).hom ≫
              (relativeKunnethMap R' cg' ch').app
                ((R'.coordinates.operations.pull G.x G.separated_x).obj K,
                 (R'.coordinates.operations.pull G.y G.separated_y).obj L)) ∧
      (∀ (Q' : SixFunctorCompactifiedSquare D) (J : RelativeKunnethClosedSquare Q Q'),
        relativeKunnethClosedFormula R J)
